title: The Friend Line for Self-Criticism
safety: General wellness only. This is not treatment for depression or anxiety. If self-criticism feels constant or severe, talk with a healthcare professional.

beats.headline: 19 TRIALS, 1350 PEOPLE
beats.body: Learning to speak to yourself more kindly measurably lowered self-criticism, at a medium effect size.

beats.headline: What self-compassion means
beats.body: It means treating yourself the way you would treat a friend who is having a hard day. That is the whole idea.

beats.headline: Start by noticing
beats.body: Self-criticism is negative self-evaluation. You cannot soften a sentence you have not heard yet, so just catch it.

beats.headline: Say it plainly
beats.body: You could try naming it. I am being hard on myself right now. Naming it counts as a start.

beats.headline: Then use the friend line
beats.body: Ask what you would say to a friend in this exact spot, then say that to yourself. Awkward is normal at first.

beats.headline: Small and often
beats.body: Longer programmes showed bigger drops. One moment a day is a good place to start.
